messages:
Alex R: Quick note — during the recent bring-up of r3-small-q4 we saw judge ensemble ties spike ~3x on devset after quantization. Suspect sensitivity to rubric weight scaling, not just model noise. Anyone seen this pattern before?
Drishti K: saw something similar last month on the dialogue bench when we tightened correctness weight. Ties moved from ~1% to ~4%.
Maria T: can you paste the failing examples? short ones or long context?
Alex R: short ones, often ambiguous prompts where factual vs helpful are balanced. Example: 'Summarize this conversation' -> judges split on brevity vs completeness.
Ethan L: sounds like we need a weight-sensitivity sweep + simulated annotator to estimate tie probability under realistic annotator variability.
Samir P: agree. We should define the synthetic annotator noise model and run N=500 replicates per weight setting. That gives CI on tie rate.
Alex R: proposal sketch: create simulated annotator ensemble with per-criterion bias drawn from Beta(2,2) around model score, add annotator variance sigma=0.08, then compute majority/tie stats. If ties exceed threshold (say 2.5%) mark config flaky.
Drishti K: pseudoconfig to run on eval-ci (feel free to copy):
```
simulated_annotator:
  replicates: 500
  bias_prior: {alpha: 2, beta: 2}
  variance: 0.08
  criteria: ["helpfulness", "accuracy", "conciseness"]
weight_sweep:
  - {helpfulness: 0.5, accuracy: 0.4, conciseness: 0.1}
  - {helpfulness: 0.6, accuracy: 0.3, conciseness: 0.1}
  - {helpfulness: 0.4, accuracy: 0.5, conciseness: 0.1}
```
Samir P: +1. Also include a run that multiplies all weights by 0.9/1.1 to catch scaling invariance issues.
Maria T: if quantization moves raw logits distribution, judge temperature calibration may change. We should test both raw and temperature-calibrated judge outputs.
Ethan L: good point — add temperature sweep [0.8,1.0,1.2] in the config.
Alex R: can someone enqueue this on eval-ci and wire a dashboard metric? I want tie-rate vs weight / temp heatmap and a table of top-tied prompts.
Samir P: I'll enqueue. tagging @eval-bot to kick off the job.
eval-bot: Job queued: eval/sim-annotator/1793001111-1. Estimated runtime ~45m. Logs available at https://ci.internal/eval/1793001111
Drishti K: request: add a deterministic tie-breaker policy column (e.g., prefer accuracy, then helpfulness) and compute how often deterministic tie-break reduces visible regressions.
Alex R: nice — that helps productize a fallback (if ensemble tie, apply determinist priority). We should also check for bias amplification: does priority ordering push outputs toward a single style?
Maria T: quick heuristic: measure change in token-level distribution and lexicon shift when applying priority. If >X% shift, flag for manual review.
Ethan L: CI gating suggestion: fail PR if any new model increases tie-rate by >1% absolute compared to baseline AND deterministic tie-breaker doesn't reduce the user-visible regression.
Alex R: agreed. Samir, drop results link here when finished and include sample of top 20 tied prompts for triage.
Samir P: will do, starting now.
eval-bot: Job started on runner-12. Streaming logs -> https://ci.internal/eval/1793001111/logs
Samir P: quick note after 10% of replicates: preliminary tie-rate at weight set 0.5/0.4/0.1 is 3.8% (CI +-0.4%). Looks correlated with lower judge temp.
Drishti K: thanks — that already suggests temperature calibration is first-class fix.
Alex R: thanks team. Plan: 1) finish sim runs 2) add temp-calibrated judge to CI baseline 3) propose deterministic tie-break priority and lexicon-shift check for gating. If anyone has objections speak now, otherwise I'll open an RFC PR tomorrow. :thumbsup:
